questions.title: Re-acknowledgment flag derivation strategy
questions.context: SPEC R3 requires `/my-policies` to render a 'Requires re-acknowledgment' badge when the user has not acked the current published version. Computation = LEFT JOIN acknowledgments ON (user_id, policy_id, policy_version_id matching current). Two implementation paths: do it in one SQL query, or split into multiple round-trips and join in app. Codebase precedent: Policies.listWithFilters is single-query with a hard LIMIT 100 (Phase 3 D-05).

options.label: Single SQL query with LEFT JOIN — derive `requiresReacknowledgment` as a SELECT expression (e.g., `CASE WHEN ack.id IS NULL AND prior.id IS NOT NULL THEN true ELSE false END`)
options.description: One round-trip; whole result set is the data the page needs. Tightest perf. Slightly denser query but mirrors Policies.listWithFilters complexity. Recommended.

options.label: Two queries — list assigned+published, then list this user's acks; join in app layer
options.description: Cleaner SQL on each side; can run via Promise.all to parallelize. App layer carries the join logic. Two RTTs instead of one.

options.label: Three queries — assignments, then policies, then acks; join in app layer
options.description: Most decomposable; each repository method does one thing. Three RTTs. Easier to unit-test each piece in isolation but slowest user-facing.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Department-less users (users.departmentId IS NULL) handling
questions.context: Schema: `users.departmentId` is nullable; a user can have NO department membership (e.g., new hire pre-assignment, contractor). SPEC R1 acceptance test seeds 4 policies including dept-assigned ones — the seeded user has a department. Real-world employee accounts may not. The query needs an answer for the null-dept case.

options.label: User-only assignments visible — WHERE clause: `(assignee_type='user' AND assignee_id=userId) OR (assignee_type='department' AND assignee_id = (SELECT department_id FROM users WHERE id=userId))`. NULL subquery silently returns no matches.
options.description: Standard SQL behavior — `assignee_id = NULL` is never true, so department-less users see only user-level assignments. No special-casing needed. Recommended.

options.label: Empty-state with helpful message — render `/my-policies` empty + 'Your administrator hasn't assigned you to a department yet'
options.description: Trades SQL elegance for explicit UX. Forces admin onboarding flow. Risks confusing users who legitimately have no policies yet.

options.label: Hard error / block page render — throw at Server Component level if departmentId is null
options.description: Strict — forces every employee to have a department. Adds complexity to onboarding. Conflicts with the existing race window (users.departmentId is settable post-webhook).

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Where the user's departmentId comes from at request time
questions.context: OrgContext currently exposes {orgId, userId, clerkOrgId, clerkUserId, role} — NO departmentId. The dashboard query needs departmentId (or a SQL-level way to derive it) to filter department-assigned policies. Three places it could come from.

options.label: Sub-select inline in the query — `... assignee_id IN (SELECT department_id FROM users WHERE id = $userId AND org_id = $orgId)`
options.description: Zero extra round-trips; OrgContext stays minimal. Database does one extra index lookup per query. Schema-encoded — RLS still fires on the inner SELECT. Recommended.

options.label: Extend OrgContext to include departmentId — getOrgContext does an additional users-row read, exposes departmentId alongside userId
options.description: Cleanest API surface; every Server Component gets departmentId for free. Adds 1 RTT to every getOrgContext call (already does 2 sequential DB reads for ADR-027). Useful beyond Phase 5 only if other surfaces need it.

options.label: Fetch fresh inside the Server Component — call Users.findByClerkUserId(s, clerkUserId) before listAssignedAndPublishedForUser
options.description: Local to /my-policies page; doesn't change OrgContext shape. Adds 1 RTT per page request. Brittle if future pages need the same data — duplication.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: IP address header source
questions.context: Schema: `acknowledgments.ip_address text` — nullable. Next.js 15 pattern: `import { headers } from 'next/headers'; const h = await headers(); h.get('x-forwarded-for')`. Vercel populates `x-forwarded-for` with the user's IP first, then proxy hops. No existing IP-capture code in this repo. SPEC R2: 'IP from x-forwarded-for first hop'.

options.label: Strict x-forwarded-for first hop — `headers().get('x-forwarded-for')?.split(',')[0]?.trim() ?? null`
options.description: Matches SPEC R2 verbatim. Single header; predictable. Vercel sets this consistently. Recommended.

options.label: Fallback chain — try `cf-connecting-ip` → `x-real-ip` → `x-forwarded-for` first hop → null
options.description: Defensive against future hosting changes (Cloudflare, custom proxy). More code; more headers to trust. Slight risk of header-spoofing via attacker-controlled cf-connecting-ip on Vercel (Vercel doesn't strip it).

options.label: x-real-ip only — single non-list header
options.description: Cleaner parsing (no split). Vercel does set it. Less standard across hosts; if we ever migrate, this breaks first.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Double-click / replay idempotency
questions.context: User clicks Acknowledge twice rapidly (or browser retries). Without a guard, both clicks insert ack rows. Schema today: no UNIQUE on acknowledgments; INSERT always succeeds. ADR-018 says append-only — but duplicate acks for the same (user, policy, version) clutter the audit trail. Coupled with Q-23.

options.label: Schema UNIQUE on (user_id, policy_id, policy_version_id) + `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`
options.description: DB-enforced idempotency. CLAUDE.md ASK FIRST — additive (no DROP), pre-paying-customer status per STATE.md. Audit-trail invariant: one ack per (user, version). Recommended; couples with Q-23(a).

options.label: Accept duplicates — every click writes a row
options.description: No schema change. Audit reports dedupe at read time. Semantically defensible ('user clicked Acknowledge at T1 and T2'). Phase 5 surface area shrinks.

options.label: App-layer SELECT-then-INSERT inside the same transaction
options.description: No schema change but race-prone unless SERIALIZABLE isolation. Two clicks landing in parallel withOrgScope transactions both see no existing row → both insert. Worst-of-both options.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Acknowledged-while-archived handling
questions.context: User loads /my-policies/{id} (status=published), admin archives between page load and click. SPEC says Draft+Under Review never appear — but the page didn't refresh. The ack click hits the action with a now-archived policy.

options.label: Reject with 400 + UI message — typed error 'This policy was archived. Refresh to update your list.'
options.description: Honest UX; tells user the world changed. Forces a refresh; the policy disappears from /my-policies after refresh (archived ≠ assigned+published). Recommended.

options.label: Allow — record the ack against the last-published version; archived state doesn't invalidate the click
options.description: Liberal write policy. Audit interpretation: 'user engaged with the policy before archival'. Could surprise audit consumers who expect acks only on published policies.

options.label: Silent no-op — return success without inserting; UI re-renders to the (now-empty) list
options.description: Lies to the user (says success when no row written). Cleanest visible UX; worst audit-trail story.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Acknowledged-while-unassigned handling
questions.context: Admin removes the policy_assignment row between page load and click. Page still shows the policy (cached render); ack click hits the action with no current assignment.

options.label: Reject with 403 + UI message — 'You are no longer assigned this policy'
options.description: Keeps audit trail honest (no ack rows for non-assigned users). Symmetric with Q-06(a) treatment. Recommended.

options.label: Allow — the user did see and engage with the policy; record the ack even if assignment was removed
options.description: Liberal write policy. Audit consumer sees 'unassigned user acked' rows — has to filter or accept. Aligns with 'click intent matters' philosophy.

options.label: Silent no-op — same UX as (a) but doesn't expose the assignment change
options.description: Lies to the user. Same cons as Q-06(c).

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Server Action file location
questions.context: Phase 3 precedent: admin Server Actions live at `app/(admin)/policies/[id]/actions.ts` co-located with the page that invokes them. Phase 4 precedent: AI endpoints live at `app/api/ai/*/route.ts` because they're HTTP-API-driven, not Server-Action-driven.

options.label: `app/(employee)/my-policies/[id]/actions.ts` — co-located with detail page
options.description: Matches Phase 3 admin precedent exactly. The action is invoked from the detail page's Acknowledge button. Recommended.

options.label: `app/(employee)/actions.ts` — shared at the route-group level
options.description: Less file scaffolding. Future-friendly if /my-policies list page ever needs an inline Acknowledge button. Slight indirection.

options.label: `lib/policies/acknowledgment.ts` — pure module + thin Server Action wrapper
options.description: Higher reuse if Phase 7 cron-reminders or future surfaces ever need to write acks. Mixes 'use server' contract with library code; Phase 3 deliberately kept these separate.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Re-ack indicator visual treatment
questions.context: SPEC R3: 'UI renders a Requires re-acknowledgment badge (visually distinct shadcn Badge variant) when requiresReacknowledgment === true AND prior acknowledgments exist'. Phase 3 ships PolicyStatusBadge (variant for each PolicyStatus). Phase 4 ships ConsistencyFindingsList with severity badges. Shadcn Badge supports custom variants via cva.

options.label: Shadcn Badge with new 'warning' variant — orange-amber background + 'Requires re-acknowledgment' text
options.description: High contrast; scannable in a list. Matches PolicyStatusBadge precedent (Phase 3). Variant can be reused for Phase 7 review-due indicators. Recommended.

options.label: Inline AlertCircle icon + small amber text — lower visual weight
options.description: Subtle; doesn't visually dominate the list. Could be missed if user scans quickly. Better for power users; worse for compliance-driven UX.

options.label: Card left-border accent (amber 4px) + small badge — highest prominence
options.description: Loud. Hard to miss. Could feel alarmist if many policies update at once. Visually heavy for compliance-officer dashboards.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: First-time ack vs re-ack differentiation
questions.context: SPEC R3: 'badge differentiates re-ack from first-time-ack; first-time acks get a plain Acknowledge CTA, not the badge'. Three patterns of how strong that differentiation should be.

options.label: Badge ONLY on re-ack — first-time = clean card with 'Acknowledge' button; re-ack = warning badge + 'Re-acknowledge' button
options.description: Per-SPEC R3 minimum; cleanest. New users see uncluttered state. Recommended.

options.label: Same UI for both — every unacknowledged version shows the same 'Acknowledge' CTA
options.description: Simpler. Conflicts with SPEC R3 wording — would require SPEC amendment.

options.label: Both badged, different colors — first-time = blue 'Action needed'; re-ack = amber 'Re-acknowledge required'
options.description: Symmetric; signals urgency on re-ack. More visual noise in a long list of new-employee assignments.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Assignment surface location
questions.context: SPEC: thin admin assignment surface on /policies/[id]. Phase 3 ships /policies/[id]/page.tsx with PolicyView + PolicyTransitionMenu. Three places to add the assign affordance.

options.label: Inline panel at bottom of /policies/[id] — dept selector + 'Assign' button below the transition menu
options.description: Single-page workflow. Admin sees policy + transitions + assignments together. Recommended.

options.label: Modal dialog triggered by 'Assign' button — shadcn Dialog with dept selector
options.description: Keeps detail page focused on policy content. Slightly more clicks per assignment. Better for low-frequency action; worse for setting up a new policy with multiple assignments.

options.label: Dedicated /policies/[id]/assignments page — full route
options.description: Future-proof for managing many assignments. Heavier; out-of-scope-feeling for Phase 5's thin scope. Decoupling forces a second navigation step.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Empty-departments UX
questions.context: Departments are created via Departments.create — currently a throw-stub (Phase 3+ admin user management). A fresh org has zero departments. Phase 5 admin tries to bulk-assign — no targets.

options.label: Disable assignment button + tooltip — 'Create a department first'; link to admin settings (when it exists)
options.description: Doesn't pretend departments are available. No risk of phantom selector. Defers department-create UX to a future phase. Recommended.

options.label: Inline 'Create department' flow — small + button next to the selector lets admin create dept inline
options.description: Lets admin do the whole flow from one page. Requires shipping Departments.create() body AND a UI affordance in Phase 5 — scope creep.

options.label: Hide assignment surface entirely until at least one department exists
options.description: Cleanest UI. Conceals the affordance — admin doesn't learn it exists until departments do. Worse discoverability.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Duplicate-assignment guard (application layer)
questions.context: Admin clicks 'Assign to Dept D' twice. Schema today has no UNIQUE on policy_assignments. App layer decides what happens. Coupled with Q-22 (schema decision).

options.label: DB UNIQUE on (policy_id, assignee_type, assignee_id) + `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`
options.description: Schema-enforced; second click is a silent no-op via UPSERT. CLAUDE.md ASK FIRST trigger (couples with Q-22(a)). SPEC R4 acceptance test 'count = 1, not N' passes naturally. Recommended.

options.label: App-layer check before insert — call PolicyAssignments.listForPolicy first; skip insert if duplicate found
options.description: No schema change. Race-prone — two parallel admin clicks both see no row, both insert. Imperfect for SPEC R4's 'exactly one row' invariant.

options.label: Accept duplicates — store both rows; query uses DISTINCT or IN
options.description: Simplest backend. Conflicts with SPEC R4 ('exactly one row'). Adds query complexity downstream.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Un-assign affordance scope
questions.context: SPEC In-Scope: 'thin admin bulk-dept-assign UI'. Out-of-Scope: 'individual-user assignment admin UI'. SPEC does NOT explicitly include or exclude un-assign.

options.label: Out of scope for Phase 5 — read-only list of assignments; un-assign deferred to a follow-up
options.description: Tightest scope. Admin gets stuck if they assign wrong dept. Workaround: edit-policy + re-publish forces re-ack on the new version anyway. Recommended (minimum-viable).

options.label: In scope — same surface gets a 'Remove' button + confirm dialog; deletes policy_assignments row
options.description: Symmetric with assign. Introduces the only DELETE in the assignment path. Code is small but adds a delete-confirm dialog + test coverage.

options.label: In scope but soft-delete only — add `revokedAt` column to policy_assignments + filter on it
options.description: Most audit-friendly (preserves history). Bigger schema change. Slippery slope toward 'why don't acks have revokedAt too'.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Gate implementation approach
questions.context: SPEC R5 requires a new ts-morph-grade CI gate forbidding `.update(acknowledgments)` / `.delete(acknowledgments)` outside the type-test fixture. Codebase precedents: scripts/check-policy-id-brand.ts + check-error-discipline.ts use ts-morph for type-aware AST traversal; scripts/check-artifacts.ts uses regex with comment-stripping (PR #7 ADR-027 pattern).

options.label: ts-morph AST traversal — Project.addSourceFilesAtPaths, walk CallExpression nodes, check method-chain against the `acknowledgments` schema import
options.description: Type-aware. Resilient to formatting / comment shifts. Catches `s.tx.update(acknowledgments)` even with whitespace variations. Recommended.

options.label: Regex with comment-stripping — strip `//` and `/* */` then test `\.update\(acknowledgments\)|\.delete\(acknowledgments\)`
options.description: Lighter dep footprint (no ts-morph in this script — but ts-morph already installed). Misses aliased imports (e.g., `import { acknowledgments as ack }`). Faster to read.

options.label: Hybrid — ts-morph for repository file + lib/policies/transitions.ts; regex sweep for everything else
options.description: Most thorough. Two code paths to maintain. Premature optimization given Phase 5's small surface.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Scope of the scan
questions.context: The repository (lib/db/repositories/acknowledgments.ts) is the only legitimate site for any write to `acknowledgments`. Other files importing the schema would be caught by Phase 2's check-db-imports.ts (raw-db allow-list). Question: how wide a net does this gate cast?

options.label: Whole `lib/**/*.ts` excluding tests/types.ts fixture + tests/fixtures/* — broad sweep
options.description: Defense-in-depth: catches any future code that smuggles in a write via a helper module or orchestrator. Recommended.

options.label: Repository file only (`lib/db/repositories/acknowledgments.ts`)
options.description: Tightest. Relies on check-db-imports.ts to keep `acknowledgments` schema-import out of other files. Two gates layered.

options.label: Whole repo `**/*.ts` excluding tests/ + scripts/ — most paranoid
options.description: Catches even app/(admin)/policies/[id]/actions.ts (no legit reason to write acks there). Most coverage; some false-positive risk on intentional dev fixtures.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Negative-control fixture wiring
questions.context: SPEC R5 acceptance requires the gate to exit non-zero against a deliberately-violating fixture — proves the gate is non-vacuous. Phase 4 precedent: check:ai-prompts has scratch/probe.ts to verify prompts work; check-ai-layer runs as vitest. Phase 2 precedent: check-rls seeds a TEST DB and rolls back.

options.label: Sibling fixture under `tests/fixtures/ack-mutation-attempt.ts` + spawn the gate as subprocess; assert non-zero exit
options.description: End-to-end smoke. Verifies the actual binary catches the violation. Mirrors Phase 4 SDK→SPEC translator test pattern. Recommended.

options.label: Vitest unit test with inline-string fixture — gate exposes a testable function; test passes a TS source string and asserts the verdict
options.description: Faster (no subprocess). Requires the gate's logic to be exportable. Tests the logic; doesn't test the CLI wiring.

options.label: No negative-control test — trust the gate code
options.description: Lightest weight. Risk: gate could break silently (e.g., a refactor that drops the actual scan call). Phase 5 SPEC R5 acceptance explicitly demands proof of non-vacuous — option (c) doesn't satisfy SPEC.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Vitest organization for Phase 5 tests
questions.context: Phase 3 precedent: lib/policies/state-machine.test.ts and lib/auth/bootstrap-errors.test.ts are co-located with source. Phase 4 precedent: scripts/check-ai-layer.test.ts is centralized at scripts/. SPEC R1/R3/R4 require integration tests against real DB.

options.label: Co-located unit tests + scripts/ integration tests — `lib/db/repositories/acknowledgments.test.ts` (unit, mocked) + `scripts/check-employee-portal.ts` (integration, real TEST DB)
options.description: Matches both Phase 3 (co-located units) and Phase 4 (scripts integration) precedents. Recommended.

options.label: Centralized under `tests/phase-5/` — all Phase-5-specific tests live in one dir; integration vs unit by file naming
options.description: Easy to scope verify:phase-5. Diverges from Phase 3 layout pattern. New convention to maintain.

options.label: All co-located — even integration tests live next to the file under test; vitest config separates by extension
options.description: Strictest co-location. Integration tests pollute source dirs (real-DB tests can be slow; co-locating signals they're not pure unit).

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Integration test DB strategy
questions.context: SPEC R1 acceptance test seeds 4 policies + asserts query returns exactly P1 + P2. SPEC R3 acceptance test acks v1, republishes, asserts re-ack badge. SPEC R4 asserts 3 dept members see policy. Phase 2/3 precedents: scripts/check-rls.ts and scripts/check-policies-list-filters.ts seed via postgres-js raw + ROLLBACK at end.

options.label: Raw postgres-js + BYPASSRLS seed + SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated for the test + ROLLBACK at end — matches check-rls + check-policies-list-filters precedent
options.description: Exercises RLS + schema constraints exactly as production does. Cross-org isolation testable. Slower (~1-2s per script). Recommended.

options.label: Vitest + Drizzle on TEST DB — beforeAll seeds via Drizzle, afterAll cleans; same TEST DB but cleaner API
options.description: Less raw SQL. Doesn't naturally test RLS unless you also configure jwt claims. Mixes ORM and test concerns.

options.label: Mocks for everything — vitest with vi.mock('@/lib/db') returning canned rows
options.description: Fast. Doesn't exercise RLS, FK integrity, or schema constraints. SPEC R5 cross-org isolation test (acceptance) NOT verifiable. Insufficient for SPEC.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: verify:phase-5 chain composition
questions.context: Current: `verify:phase-4 = verify:phase-3 && check:ai-prompts && check:ai-layer`. Phase 5 needs at least: typecheck, all Phase 3/4 gates, check-acknowledgment-immutability, check-employee-portal (integration test).

options.label: `pnpm verify:phase-4 && pnpm check:acknowledgment-immutability && pnpm check:employee-portal` — chain forward
options.description: Cumulative: every Phase-1-through-5 gate runs. Slowest but most defensive. Phase 4 already chains Phase 3. Recommended.

options.label: Discrete chain — `verify:phase-5 = typecheck + check:artifacts + check:ack-immutability + check:employee-portal + test`; skip Phase 3/4 gates
options.description: Fast fail signal for Phase-5-specific drift. Misses regressions in Phase 3/4 paths. Worse for ship-readiness.

options.label: Hybrid — `verify:phase-5 = verify:phase-4 && [Phase 5 gates]`; add separate `verify:phase-5-fast` for inner-loop development
options.description: Best of both. Two scripts to maintain. Inner-loop variant deviates from one-script-to-verify-a-phase convention.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: Employee-side Q&A affordance
questions.context: ROADMAP Phase 5 goal text: 'employee can ... ask Q&A questions'. ADR-029 (2026-05-21): 'Phase 5 SC 1–5 do not consume Phase 4 AI surfaces'. SPEC R-boundaries puts employee Q&A UI explicitly OUT OF SCOPE. POST /api/ai/qa exists from Phase 4 and is reachable by any authenticated user. Decision: do we hint at the future surface in /my-policies, or omit entirely?

options.label: Omit entirely — no Q&A link, button, or sidebar item in /my-policies. ADR-029 + SPEC boundaries are binding; goal-narrative reference is informational only.
options.description: Tightest. Zero scope creep. Future phase can add Q&A as a clean surface. Recommended.

options.label: Disabled placeholder link — sidebar/topbar shows 'Ask the AI' with 'Coming soon' tooltip + cursor-not-allowed
options.description: Documents future affordance. Minor scope creep (UI element shipped that does nothing). Risk: users click and feel teased.

options.label: Wire it through — ship thin /my-policies/ask page calling existing POST /api/ai/qa
options.description: Honors goal-narrative. Direct scope-creep vs ADR-029 + SPEC. Adds untested-in-Phase-5 attack surface (Q&A UI security review skipped).

options.label: Custom

questions.title: UNIQUE on policy_assignments(policy_id, assignee_type, assignee_id)
questions.context: Currently no UNIQUE on policy_assignments. SPEC R4 demands 'exactly one row' for dept assignment. CLAUDE.md ASK FIRST: schema changes after Phase 2 require operator approval. Pre-paying-customer per STATE.md → additive constraints are safe. Coupled with Q-13.

options.label: Add it — new migration `0010_policy_assignments_unique.sql` (additive). Mirror 03-G3 T2/T3 belt-and-suspenders pattern for policy_versions
options.description: Schema-enforced 'exactly one row' invariant. Phase 5 SC #4 trivially satisfied. ASK FIRST satisfied: additive + pre-customer. Recommended; couples with Q-13(a).

options.label: Skip — rely on app-layer dedup (Q-13(b)) or accept duplicates (Q-13(c))
options.description: No schema change. Phase 5 surface area smaller. Risk: SPEC R4 'exactly one row' invariant is app-enforced only — easier to regress in future phases.

options.label: Add but defer to Phase 5.5 polish — track in a follow-up issue like Phase 4 issue #16
options.description: Phase 5 ships without; backlog catches it later. Pattern works if there's a clear backlog process. Slight risk of indefinite deferral.

options.label: Custom

questions.title: UNIQUE on acknowledgments(user_id, policy_id, policy_version_id)
questions.context: Currently no UNIQUE on acknowledgments. SPEC R5 + ADR-018 says append-only; doesn't say 'one ack per version'. But duplicate acks for the same (user, version) bloat the audit trail. Coupled with Q-05.

options.label: Add it — new migration; enables `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on insert. Enforces 'one ack per (user, version)' at DB level
options.description: DB-enforced idempotency. ASK FIRST: additive + pre-customer. Couples with Q-05(a). Audit-trail invariant strengthened. Recommended.

options.label: Skip — accept duplicates; audit consumers dedupe at read time
options.description: No schema change. Couples with Q-05(b). 'Audit trail captures every click' interpretation.

options.label: Add but defer — Phase 5.5 polish
options.description: Same defer pattern as Q-22(c).

options.label: Custom
